text: RESULTS: Echocardiogram: Presence of an atrial septal defect with left to right shunt. Complete Blood Count: WBC 11,000 /μL, Hemoglobin 12 g/dL, Platelets 300,000 /μL. Urinalysis: NORMAL READINGS.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Significant rapid breathing. I also have Appears unwell, Diminished appetite, No fever, Swelling in the legs. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Glomerulonephritis.

The combination of significant edema, diminished appetite, and rapid breathing in a previously healthy 3-year-old, despite the negative initial cardiac workup, strongly suggests fluid retention secondary to renal failure rather than primary heart disease. The lack of fever and cough further supports a non-infectious etiology like post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis.
